Simulator & explorer

Three live tools from the Spotle opener research: look up exactly how any guess would split the field, re-rank the best openers using only the clues you personally trust, or simulate how many guesses it'd actually take to land on a specific movie. Everything below runs live in your browser against the same 3,000-film pool as the research — nothing is precomputed.

01Explore any guess yourself

Pick any film in the pool, or build a hypothetical guess from scratch, and see exactly how each clue would split the field — e.g. "guessing a 2005 movie produces this many gray-down-arrow results, this many yellow-down-arrow, this many green." Everything below is computed live in your browser against all 3,000 films, not precomputed.

Start typing and choose a suggestion, or use a quick pick above.
Genres (select any)
Cast (optional, up to 5)

Leave any field blank to skip that clue entirely — its breakdown just won't be shown. Director/studio/cast autocomplete against real names in the pool since matching is by exact name.

Choose a film or build a custom guess to see its breakdown…

02Simulate with only the clues you trust

The research assumes you're using all 8 clues. If a clue is worthless to you personally — say, you never recognize distributors, so Studio tells you nothing useful even when it's green — turn it off below and the ranking recomputes using only what's left, live in your browser. You can also restrict the whole simulation to just the N most popular films, as if that were Spotle's entire library — useful if you suspect the daily answer always skews toward well-known titles.

most popular films (of 3,000)
Rank by:

All 8 clues selected — this matches the full ranking in the research.

03How many guesses would it take?

Pick a movie that was actually the answer and this plays out the whole game against it: an optimal opener, then whichever guess is best among what's left, turn after turn, until it lands on the target — the same methodology as the research above, live in your browser.

Optimize the opening guess for:

Only the opener changes between the two — every guess after the first always greedily picks whichever candidate leaves the fewest films remaining, the same “greedy continuation” the research uses throughout (a fully exhaustive search isn't feasible in-browser).
